messages:
alex: seeing weird pod-to-pod failures in gpu-training — jobs hitting RDMA errors and a bunch of retransmits. p95 latency between nodes jumped from 3ms -> 80ms after yesterday's change :eyes:
june: ugh. is this the netpol change mike rolled out?
alex: looks like it. I see a NetworkPolicy named `gpuegress-deny` applied to gpu-training, blocks egress except to svc discovery. ran `kubectl get netpol gpuegress-deny -n gpu-training -o yaml` and it has an egress deny with IPBlock and no rules for hostNetwork or other namespaces.
mike: yeah that was my quick containment for noisy tenants — intended to block external egress, not pod-to-pod. i thought calico would allow intra-ns by default but i must've been too strict. my bad.
ryan_oncall: can we quickly confirm whether traffic is actually being dropped vs MTU/fragmentation? RDMA (RoCE) is sensitive to dropped fragmented packets. try `iperf3 -s` on node A and `iperf3 -c` node B, and `tcpdump -i any 'ether proto 0x8915 or udp'` to capture RoCE/UDP frames.
june: ran `iperf3 -c` between gpu-node-3 -> gpu-node-7: `-u` UDP test shows ~9% packet loss; TCP test had high retransmits too. when i forced MTU=1500 on both NICs loss went to 0%. but our cluster normally uses jumbo (9000).
alex: interesting — netpol shouldn't change MTU. but I also see conntrack spikes on the node where policy applied: `conntrack -S` shows entries jumping into the hundreds of thousands.
mike: the netpol has an IPBlock with except: ranges and uses podSelector: {} for targets. maybe calico implemented it by adding host-level egress hooks that hit conntrack and cause fragmentation?
infra-bot: calico-controller reported "PolicyUpdateFailed: policy gpuegress-deny created in gpu-training caused route programming delay" at 2026-03-18T14:02:11Z
ryan_oncall: quick mitigation: add an allow rule for `podSelector: {}` egress to namespace gpu-training CIDR and specifically add `ports: [{protocol: "UDP", port: 4791}]` used by RoCE shim, plus allow ICMP fragmentation reassembly. also add `egress: - to: [{namespaceSelector: {matchLabels: {name: kube-system}}}]`? we should keep it minimal.
june: i pushed a small patch to netpol to explicitly allow intra-namespace pod-to-pod, and allowed ICMP type 3 code 4 (fragmentation needed). rolling now.
mike: rolling back my deny warmed up — sorry for the noise. i'll add a checklist before netpol deploys next time (PM me).
alex: after the patch p95 lat dropped back to ~4ms, RDMA errors disappeared in dmesg, iperf3 UDP loss -> 0. I saved packet captures to /var/tmp/gpu-netpol-rcap.pcap for postmortem.
june: raising a follow-up doc and small postmortem. action items: (1) add netpol review checklist (2) test RoCE and MTU invariants in staging (3) add integration test: apply default-deny and run iperf/rdma smoke.
ryan_oncall: created incident INC-2026-187 and linked the netpol PR. marking as resolved for now, will reopen if we see any regressions. :white_check_mark:
mike: apologies again. i'll coordinate on a safer policy rollout and include knockout tests for jumbo frames.
alex: thanks everyone — feel free to ping if this resurfaces.
